notes: Holy priest healer rotation, written against the fork's fake raid: the healer is raid player 0, the four fake party members are players 1 to 4 and the tank is player 5. Reference build: 35 points in Holy and 16 in Discipline (engine talent string 0052030312-33505003030121531: Improved Renew, Holy Specialization, Divine Fury 5, Inspiration, Improved Healing, Holy Binding (Binding Heal until client 1.60.1.70707), Litany of Light 2, Spirit of Redemption, Spiritual Guidance 5, Spiritual Healing, Prayer of Mending; Twin Disciplines 5, Improved Power Word: Shield, Silent Resolve 2, Mental Agility 3, Inner Focus, Meditation 2). The tank carries Prayer of Mending and Renew; everyone else is healed reactively by health share, with Heal as the filler and Flash Heal / Prayer of Healing for the moments that need them. Mana: the list opens with the autocast line, which is how the Major Mana Potion, the Demonic Rune and Inner Focus are used (each fires whenever it is ready and the bar has room for it; Inner Focus goes on whichever priest spell is cast next). Dark Sacrifice follows the autocast line behind a mana gate (below 70% mana with the healer's own health above 70%). Mana pacing: the non-emergency lines (Heal filler, Prayer of Healing) fire at their normal thresholds only while the mana bar is at least 90% of the share of the fight left (currentManaPercent against remainingTimePercent); behind that pace the filler waits for a tank under 50% and a member under 35%. Prayer of Mending, Renew on the tank and the emergency Flash Heals are never paced. Ranks follow one rule, stated in design/reviews/2026-10-08-healer-mana-audit.md: starting from the top ranks, a lower rank (never one learned below level 20) is taken for a spell when it raises the ranker's guarded score by more than two percent, the biggest gain first, the tank's casts and the party members' casts counted apart, and compared on the raid gear the ranker published for the list being tried. The engine states the client's own numbers for every rank with no downrank penalty, so a lower rank is a statement about this profile, not a measurement of the game. The site runs this list as written at band 60; below 60 each ranked spell casts the highest rank learned that is not above the rank named here, unless data/curated/rank-choices.json names another rank for the band (owner ruling 3, sim-accuracy round 9). Here that is Renew on the tank at rank 3 and, since round 9, Flash Heal on the tank at rank 2; every other spell keeps the top rank a trainer teaches (Prayer of Healing rank 5 and Renew rank 10 are Ahn'Qiraj book ranks, so their tops in Phase 1 are ranks 4 and 9; Heal stops at rank 4). The comparison is repeated on the gear each new list makes the ranker choose until no spell moves. The review lists what each rank returned. Round-3 audit (design/reviews/2026-11-01-sim-audit-round3/casters.md): Shadowfiend (401977) is not cast; a Forever priest cannot learn it (no learn level on its skill-line row, and no beta priest ever cast it). Lightwell is placed before the pull (a prepull cast, 365 mana at rank 3): the fake raid members the damage model hurts click it for a renew each, five charges, and its client rows are 320 health every 2 seconds for 10 seconds that being attacked cancels, so over the profile it returned about 0.4 percent more effective healing and 3.6 more seconds of mana than the same list without it (spec-breakdown -heal, 2026-10-08, design/reviews/2026-10-08-remaining-trainables.md).

priorityList.notes: Dark Sacrifice, Undead only, once you are under 70% mana and still healthy: it turns your own health into mana over 15 seconds, plus your Spirit, and its 10 minute cooldown makes it once a fight.

Prayer of Mending on the tank every time it is ready: up to five heals for one cast on a 10 second cooldown, the cheapest healing you can cast all fight. It heals whoever holds it on their next hit or direct heal, and the tank is hit and healed the most. It is not held back by the mana pace the costlier heals follow: it is the last heal to give up when mana runs short.
Keep Renew on the tank all fight; at 60 that means rank 7 or higher.
Prayer of Healing once three of your four party members are under 85%: it heals the target and the target's whole party.
Greater Heal is the filler while your mana keeps pace with the fight: rank 1 until 60, then rank 3 or your top trainer rank, which heal about the same for their mana.
When your mana falls behind the fight, only on a tank under 50% or a party member under 35%, so it waits for a deeper hole.
Once you have higher ranks, when the top rank would overheal or your mana runs short: it costs far less and still keeps most of your healing bonus at 60.
When your mana falls behind the fight, only on a tank under 50% or a party member under 35%, so it waits for a deeper hole too.

Heal is the step down when Greater Heal rank 1 costs more than you can spend, and your filler before Greater Heal at 40. Below 34 cast rank 1, though some races cast rank 2 or 3 at a few levels, since it keeps your whole healing bonus until then and heals the most for its mana. Rank 2 or 3 takes over at 28 and 32 for most races, at 27 for a Human, Gnome or Night Elf, and at 30 and 31 for an Undead or Troll. Rank 4 costs more mana than its extra healing is worth in its first levels, so keep rank 3 from 34 to 37 and to 38 as an Undead; a Troll stays on rank 1 at 34 and casts rank 2 at 38 and 39, and an Undead casts rank 2 at 39. From 40 Greater Heal is your main heal; fall back to Heal rank 4 only when you are short of mana for Greater Heal rank 1, since rank 4 is cheaper but keeps only about half your bonus at 60.
When your mana falls behind the fight, only on a tank under 50% or a party member under 35%, so it waits for a deeper hole.
Lesser Heal is your filler until you learn Heal at 16: rank 3, on the tank first and on the party once they are low. Pace your mana the way you will with Heal.
